title: Juniper and the Will
premise: Tamsin Lockridge, a concierge at the decaying Grand Meridian Hotel, receives two letters after a guest's drowning: one confessing to murder, one promising her an inheritance she never knew existed. Following the dead man's trail through the hotel's ledgers, she discovers her own name woven through decades of transactions — evidence that the Lockridge family fortune was built on a crime that erased her mother's identity. As the tide gives up what it took and the true heir closes in, Tamsin must choose between claiming the corrupted inheritance or burning it. In the end she exposes the killer at the hotel's centennial gala, refuses the will, and walks out owning only what she can carry.
about_author: O. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former night auditor who spent eleven years watching strangers check in and out of coastal hotels. They write mysteries about the people behind front desks — those who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Signed in Rain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A nervous guest named Edmund Vane checks into the Grand Meridian during a storm, asking odd questions about the hotel's founding family. Tamsin notices his wet shoes, his false name on the register, and the way he flinches at the portrait of old Ambrose Lockridge. Emotional beat: unease — her instincts say this man is running from something, or toward it.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vane is found drowned below the sea wall; police call it accidental. Days later two letters arrive for Tamsin: one confessing to a murder, unsigned but in Vane's hand; one promising 'what the Lockridges owe you.' She hides both from Detective Sorrel. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion — she cannot stop reading them.

chapters.title: Everything the Front Desk Knows
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She reconstructs Vane's stay from keycard logs, bar tabs, and the switchboard: he met someone in Room 412 the night he died. The room belonged to a guest registered as 'M. Ashcombe' who checked out before dawn. Emotional beat: the quiet thrill of competence — noticing is what Tamsin is for.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching the hotel archive for Lockridge history, she finds the centennial guest ledger where certain entries form a pattern — dates and room numbers encoding sums of money paid out yearly since 1971. Emotional beat: vertigo. The hotel she thought she knew has been keeping a second set of books all along.

chapters.title: Detective Sorrel's Patience
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The detective interviews Tamsin, revealing Vane's real identity: Julian Pryce, an archivist who had been researching the Lockridge estate. Sorrel suspects Tamsin knows more than she says. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; two careful observers circling each other, neither willing to show their cards first.

chapters.title: What the Will Says About Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Through a probate clerk, she learns Ambrose Lockridge's will contains a sealed codicil naming an unnamed beneficiary 'of the housekeeper's line.' Her grandmother was the Lockridges' housekeeper. Emotional beat: grief and anger braided together — her erased family history suddenly has a paper trail.

chapters.title: Room 412 Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She breaks into the long-shuttered Room 412 and finds Pryce's hidden notes: proof that in 1971, Ambrose's wife faked a death at sea to escape him, and the annual ledger payments were hush money to keep it buried. Emotional beat: revelation as violation — the truth was sleeping one floor above her all along.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Checks In
chapters.summary: Marcus Lockridge's POV. Ambrose's grandson arrives to sell the failing hotel, charming staff and press alike. Privately he is hunting the ledger, which proves the fortune he's selling is built on fraud — and hunting whoever Pryce told. Emotional beat: cold ambition; Marcus is the novel's polished, patient antagonist.

chapters.title: An Offer Over Cold Tea
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin/Marcus POV. Marcus offers Tamsin a generous severance and a warning about 'troublemakers,' making clear he knows about the letters. Tamsin plays dumb while confirming he had access to Vane's mail. Emotional beat: masked hostility across a tea tray; both know, neither says.

chapters.title: The Confession Reread
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Forensic attention to the confession letter reveals it names not Vane's own crime but one he witnessed: the 1971 'drowning' was staged by the family lawyer, Aldous Crane, still alive and resident in the hotel's penthouse. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything — the letter wasn't a confession, it was a message meant for her.

chapters.title: Penthouse Ghost
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. The dying old lawyer reflects on the crime he arranged and the payments he administered, aware someone has been in the archives. He burns a page of his private copy of the ledger. Emotional beat: decayed conscience; guilt that has calcified into self-justification over fifty years.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At extreme low tide, the sea exposes the base of the old sea wall — and a rusted strongbox matching the 1971 police report's missing evidence. Before she can reach it, someone watches from the cliff path. Emotional beat: race against the tide made literal; hope and exposure in equal measure.

chapters.title: Sorrel Catches Up
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The detective confronts Tamsin with the letters, forcing a partial alliance: Sorrel admits the drowning is now treated as suspicious, and Tamsin shares the ledger pattern but keeps the codicil secret. Emotional beat: wary trust — two investigators deciding, almost simultaneously, to risk each other.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Sorrel's POV. They recover the box: inside, the original 1971 death certificate draft marked FICTITIOUS, and photographs proving Ambrose's wife lived on under a new name — the name Tamsin's mother carried. Emotional beat: shattering recognition; Tamsin isn't chasing the mystery, she is its living remainder.

chapters.title: Mother's Line
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In her grandmother's belongings, she finds letters from Ambrose's wife explaining the bargain: silence and a new identity in exchange for the annual payments, cut off when Tamsin's mother tried to go public. Emotional beat: mourning retroactive — generations of women erased by a signature and a tide.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Someone torches the hotel archive; the master ledger survives only because Tamsin photographed it. Marcus realizes Crane is destroying evidence to protect himself, and that Tamsin holds copies. Emotional beat: escalation — alliances fracture, and the quiet crime becomes a live threat.

chapters.title: Crane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She finds Crane dead in the penthouse, staged as suicide, with a final ledger line entered in his trembling hand: a payment dated the night of Vane's death — received by M. Lockridge. Emotional beat: cold fury; the pattern has claimed another life, and now points unambiguously at Marcus.

chapters.title: The Centennial Gala
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Marcus hosts the hotel's centennial ball to announce the sale, planning to bury the past with champagne. Tamsin, invited as staff, wears her grandmother's restored housekeeper's brooch — the codicil's token — into the lion's den. Emotional beat: coiled anticipation; the trap is set, but who is catching whom.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV (climax). During the toast, Tamsin publicly reads the ledger entries and the forged certificate, while Sorrel arrests Marcus as he tries to flee through the service corridors — corridors Tamsin knows better than anyone. Emotional beat: cathartic reversal; the invisible woman makes the whole room see.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returned
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The investigation closes: Marcus charged, Crane's fifty-year fraud unraveled, Vane/Pryce posthumously vindicated as the man who tried to tell the truth. Sorrel offers Tamsin the case file and an apology for doubting her. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; justice arrives imperfect but arrived.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The probate court validates the codicil: the Lockridge residue is hers. Standing in the grand lobby, Tamsin declines the inheritance, directing it instead to fund the hotel's staff pension fund and a memorial to the woman the sea never really took. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; power refused is identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Concierge, Off Duty
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, Tamsin checks out of the Grand Meridian herself, leaving the two letters with Sorrel and taking only her grandmother's brooch. On the platform she opens a fresh notebook and writes a single entry — her own name, her own date, nothing owed. Emotional beat: quiet, open-ended freedom; the observer finally steps into her own story.
